title: C1687 — Front brake pad wear sensor LH
introduction:
I use this reference like an address book for the connector: identify the housing, find a cavity in the drawing, then read across its matching table row. The identity table describes the connector; the pin table connects cavity labels with circuits and their recorded functions; the pigtail table identifies the listed service assembly.

The drawing has an elongated, rounded housing outline with projections above and along its left side. Those features help distinguish the drawing, but their release or locking functions are not identified. This is a guide to reading the reference, not an access, probing or replacement procedure. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of the Size and Used codes are unspecified; I leave those fields uninterpreted.

edits.why: I use the vertically arranged cavity labels to connect the drawing with the pin table below. Upper and lower describe positions on this illustration, without establishing which side of a physical connector to view.

edits.text: Read the cavity and circuit assignments
edits.why: Start at Cavity and read across the same row for Circuit Number, Color, Gauge and Function. Keep the left-front and right-front function descriptions distinct: the LH title alone cannot explain how those circuits relate. A blank Qualifier adds no stated condition, and an unavailable terminal part number is not a replacement recommendation.

I cross-check the identity table's Kit List against Number here, then compare Hard Shell with Engineering Shell. Service Part identifies the listed pigtail assembly. Its Gauge field belongs to that assembly; it does not authorize substituting wire for the circuit-table entry.
